target.body:
## Summary
Remove the dead `securityCLIReadOverride` process-global test-override static
(`ClaudeOAuthCredentials` / `+TestingOverrides` / `+SecurityCLIReader`) together with its unused
`setSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting` setter. Its test call sites already use the task-local
`withSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting` scope; the static + setter were the leftover process-global.

## Changes
- Delete `nonisolated(unsafe) static var securityCLIReadOverride` + `setSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting(_:)`.
- Drop the dead `taskLocal ?? static` / `|| static != nil` fallback from the three readers
  (`currentSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting`, the `SecurityCLIReader` override check, and the
  `ClaudeOAuthCredentials` persistent-ref guard). The `@TaskLocal taskSecurityCLIReadOverride`, its
  `with…` scopes, and the `TestingOverridesSnapshot` machinery are untouched.

## Validation
- `make check` → 0 violations / 1465 files.
- Full suite, contract config (`GROUP_SIZE=4 TIMEOUT=120 RETRY=0`): **660 selections / 165 groups,
  first-pass 165/165, 0 failed, 0 retries, 0 timeouts** (639s).
- Static verification: `setSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting` has **zero callers** repo-wide (`rg`);
  the static was written only inside it, so production only ever read the default `nil`. Tests drive the
  live path via `withSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting` (10+ sites).

## Why safe / no behavioral delta
The static was never written outside the (now-removed, uncalled) setter, so no reader saw a non-nil
value — pure dead-seam removal. Unlike #2239's statics this one is module-`internal` (not `private`), so
it had cross-file readers within `CodexBarCore` (the SecurityCLIReader override check, the persistent-ref
guard) — all traced and updated; no readers remain.

## Related
- Part of https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2204 · follows #2239 (PR1).

## Out of scope
- Remaining #2204 seams (`fingerprintProviderOverride`, `CookieHeaderCache`, `KeychainAccessGate`) — separate PRs.
- No account/auth-file behavior changes. Screenshots not applicable (non-UI).

## Notes
- No CHANGELOG entry — internal test synchronization only.


## Real-behavior proof

Fresh build from this PR head (`c776132`), then the focused SecurityCLI-reader suites — which drive the real Claude OAuth security-CLI read path (success, timeout, and non-zero-exit fallback branches) — pass with the process-global removed. Swift 6.3.3, arm64 macOS.

**Zero remaining references to the removed static + setter** (repo-wide); the task-local scope is the sole override path:

```
$ grep -rn "setSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting" Sources Tests
(no matches — 0 call sites)
$ grep -rn "nonisolated(unsafe) static var securityCLIReadOverride" Sources
(no matches — static removed)
$ grep -rl "withSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting" Tests | wc -l   # surviving task-local scope sites
11
```

(The retained `TestingOverridesSnapshot.securityCLIReadOverride` struct field and the `currentSecurityCLIReadOverrideForTesting()` reader are intentionally untouched — only the `nonisolated(unsafe)` static + its setter were removed.)

**Freshly built + focused SecurityCLI-reader execution:**

```
$ swift test --filter "SecurityCLI"
Build complete! (85.26s)
… warning …claude-usage: error_type=SecurityCLIReadError reader=securityCLI reason=timedOut … falling back
… warning …claude-usage: error_type=SecurityCLIReadError reader=securityCLI reason=nonZeroExit status=1 … falling back
✔ Test run with 23 tests in 3 suites passed after 0.036 seconds.
```

The `SecurityCLIReadError … falling back` lines are the suites deliberately exercising the reader's timeout / non-zero-exit fallback paths — i.e. the security-CLI read path runs end-to-end against the built module. 23/23 pass; removing the dead static changes no reader behavior.

target.title: Add shareable subscription usage cards
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar already computes local token and estimated-cost history, but the menu is a poor sharing surface: the numbers cannot be copied as one artifact, and a menu screenshot is fragile and difficult to read. This PR turns the existing local data into a fixed 1200x630 card plus a plain-text equivalent.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local export**, not a hosted profile:

- no account system, public URL, upload, tracking, or backend;
- no prompt, project, path, email, or account identity in the payload;
- no attempt to make unlike measurements look complete; unknown spend remains unknown;
- one immutable payload drives preview, PNG, clipboard text, and saved image.

Alternatives considered:

- **Screenshot the current menu:** clips, changes size, and mixes controls with the artifact.
- **Hosted share link / OG page:** introduces persistence, deletion, abuse, and privacy-policy work that is not justified for v1.
- **Provider-by-provider exports:** fails the core use case of comparing all enabled AI subscriptions in one picture.

## What this adds

- A native **Share Stats...** action in the status menu and Settings -> Menu -> Sharing.
- A 1200x630 local card with combined 30-day tracked tokens and estimated spend.
- Distinct ranked subscription rows with readable inline plan names and a three-model ranking.
- A ten-bucket activity strip whose colors reinforce the named subscription rows.
- OpenRouter API-key spend surfaced as explicitly labeled month-to-date data rather than hidden or mixed into the trailing-period total.
- **Copy Image**, **Copy Stats**, and **Save...** actions from one preview.
- Existing CodexBar typography, localization patterns, menu descriptors, and lifecycle handling.

## Permission and prompt boundary

The feature adds no entitlement, system permission request, network request, background upload, or automatic pasteboard write.

| User action | Side effect |
| --- | --- |
| Open Share Stats | Reads in-memory provider snapshots and configured local Codex history only. No prompt is presented. |
| Copy Image | Writes PNG/TIFF data to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Copy Stats | Writes plain text to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Save... | Presents the standard save panel only after the explicit button press. |

Sibling Codex-account history uses the account homes already represented in CodexBar settings. A missing, unreadable, or timed-out history source degrades to an unpriced connected row; the sharing flow does not request broad filesystem access to compensate.

## Account-complete data contract

| Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tracked tokens | Sum of known local token-history snapshots in the selected 30-day window. |
| Estimated spend | Sum of finite priced history only; the card reports priced-source coverage. |
| Codex subscriptions | One identity-free row per visible Codex account, labeled `Codex · #1`, `Codex · #2`, etc. |
| Other subscriptions | One row per enabled provider source. Missing local history reads `connected`, never `$0`. |
| OpenRouter spend | Uses the existing in-memory `keyUsageMonthly` value, labels it `MTD`, and reports it separately from trailing-30-day totals. |
| Top models | Cross-provider aggregation of real model breakdowns or model names for the same window; each row names its provider. |
| Activity strip | Tracked tokens grouped into at most ten time buckets and stacked by named subscription. |

The active Codex account reuses the normal provider snapshot. Each sibling account scans its own Codex home into a separate hashed cache, with Pi session history disabled for sibling scans so shared Pi history is counted exactly once. Account scan failures degrade to connected/unpriced rows rather than deleting a visible subscription.

## Readability and accessibility

- The card is designed and checked at its 600 x 315 feed render, not only at the 1200 x 630 export size.
- Essential labels start at 18 pt native; subscription and model names use 20 pt. Tiny plan pills and model-mapping microcopy were removed.
- Every provider and model association uses a name and two-digit rank in addition to a compact color locator.
- Against the warm near-black background, primary text measures 16.5:1, secondary text 8.1:1, and the OpenRouter accent 7.8:1.
- The exported artifact is static and does not depend on motion or hover state.
- The sourced standards, Exa/Parallel comparison, and OpenRouter frontier-model panel are documented in [the readability review](docs/share-card-readability-review-2026-07-13.md).

## Privacy allowlist

The export payload permits provider display name, plan label, aggregate tokens, aggregate estimated cost, active-day counts, model name, period end, and per-subscription daily aggregate token counts. It does not carry email, account ID, project name/path, prompt text, session title, file content, credentials, or raw event records. Rendering and pasteboard/save operations are local.

## Current configured-bundle proof

These images come from a freshly compiled, signed local app bundle using the contributor's real configured aggregate data. The payload contains no account identity, prompts, projects, paths, endpoints, or credentials.

![Current real-bundle share card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-bundle.png)

![Current real-bundle preview after Copy Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-preview.png)

Observed behavior:

- The production preview surfaced four named subscriptions, three named models, a 30-day estimate, and a separate OpenRouter MTD figure.
- Clicking the preview's real **Copy Image** action produced a 1200 x 630 pasteboard item with `public.png` and `public.tiff` representations; the preview status changed to `Image copied`.
- Clicking **Copy Stats** produced 610 characters containing the live subscription names, model-provider mappings, OpenRouter MTD amount, and local-generation provenance.
- No screen-recording permission was granted or required. The proof image was recovered from CodexBar's own clipboard export path.

## Relationship to the Settings dashboard

- Companion PR: [#2116 - Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2116)
- This PR owns the share/export workflow only.
- #2116 owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime.

## Verification

- [x] Incremental arm64 release build after the feed-readability redesign
- [x] Exact 1200 x 630 production view exported and visually inspected at both native and 600 x 315 feed size
- [x] Real configured-bundle Copy Image and Copy Stats paths exercised through the preview controls
- [x] Primary, secondary, and accent contrast measured at 16.5:1, 8.1:1, and 7.8:1
- [x] No new entitlement, dependency, network path, or automatic pasteboard behavior
- [ ] Real configured-bundle Save... confirmation
- [x] `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` - 8 focused tests passed
- [x] `make check` - localization, formatting, SwiftLint, shell/docs/package gates passed
- [x] Fresh sharded test suite in GitHub CI

The local widget-packaging step is blocked by an installed Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plug-in mismatch. This is machine-local; the CodexBar target builds cleanly, and GitHub CI is the authoritative full-suite result. The focused share-stat suite passes locally, including privacy-label and shared-calendar-window regressions. GitHub CI remains the authoritative full-suite result.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. This PR asks maintainers to approve a permanent, privacy-first local usage-card export that includes every visible subscription without exposing account identity or adding permission prompts.

target.title: feat: add codexbar guard — quota-aware exit code to gate automation
target.body:
Implements the proposal in #2235. Opening it with the code + proof rather than waiting, since it's small and self-contained — happy to iterate on the flag shape or close it if the direction isn't wanted.

## Summary
Adds `codexbar guard` — a quota-aware exit code that turns CodexBar from a passive display into a guardrail scripts and agent loops can gate on.

```
codexbar guard --provider <id> [--need <percent>] [--window session|weekly] [--json] [--fail-open]
```
- Exit `0` = safe (relevant window has ≥ `--need`% remaining), `1` = insufficient headroom, `2` = unknown/unreachable.
- `--need` defaults to 10. `--window` defaults to `session` (primary window); `weekly` checks the secondary.
- `--fail-open` exits `0` instead of `2` when quota is unknown.

```bash
# don't start the next agent iteration if you can't finish it
while codexbar guard --provider claude --need 15; do run-agent-iteration; done
# gate a long task
codexbar guard --provider codex --need 30 && ./long-task.sh
```

## Design
- The gating decision is a pure function, `evaluateGuard(remainingPercent:needPercent:failOpen:)`, kept free of I/O so it's unit-testable off-network.
- The fetch reuses the existing single-provider pipeline (`ProviderFetchContext` → `fetchProviderUsage`), run under `.background` interaction (no Keychain prompts), exactly like `usage`.
- No new UI, no changes to existing behavior — purely additive.

## Tests
`TestsLinux/CLIGuardDecisionTests.swift` — 5 deterministic cases: ample→ok/0, insufficient→blocked/1, unknown→2, unknown+fail-open→0, boundary (remaining == need)→ok/0.

## Verification (Linux, `swift:6.3.3`)
```
$ swift build --product CodexBarCLI
Build of product 'CodexBarCLI' complete! (29.63s)

$ swift test --filter CLIGuardDecision
✔ Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.001 seconds.

$ codexbar guard --provider claude --need 10 --fail-open
claude session: unknown — UNKNOWN (need 10%)          # exit 0
$ codexbar guard --provider claude --need 10
claude session: unknown — UNKNOWN (need 10%)          # exit 2
$ codexbar guard --provider claude --need 10 --json --fail-open
{"exitCode":0,"window":"session","needPercent":10,"provider":"claude","decision":"unknown"}   # exit 0
```
Built and tested on Linux (`swift:6.3.3`); the macOS CI job validates the cross-platform build.



---

## Review feedback addressed (clawsweeper, commit `4d06f796`)
Both P2 findings fixed:
1. **Account resolution** (`CLIGuardCommand.swift`) — `guard` now resolves the configured token account via `resolvedAccounts(for:).first` and threads it through the fetch (env/settings/source/context), matching `usage`. Token-only Claude/z.ai/OpenAI configs now return a real decision instead of `unknown`.
2. **Synthetic-window filtering** — window selection goes through a pure `guardRemainingHeadroom(for:)` that returns `nil` for a `nil` or `isSyntheticPlaceholder` window, so a phantom primary (e.g. Claude with no live 5-hour session) is treated as `unknown` rather than a false `100%`-available exit `0`.

Added 4 regression tests for the window-headroom path (real / synthetic / absent / fully-used) — 9 guard tests total. Verified in `swift:6.3.3`: swiftlint `--strict` 0 violations, swiftformat `--lint` clean, `CodexBarCLI` builds, 9/9 tests pass.

Still open for the maintainer (not contributor-fixable): (a) real known-quota terminal proof of safe/blocked from a configured account, and (b) product sign-off on the public flag/exit-code contract.

target.title: fix(claude): preserve last-good snapshot across CLI probe failures (fixes #2241)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2241 by preserving the last-good Claude usage snapshot across two failure paths that currently clear it:

1. **Subscription-only probe responses** on accounts that already have a Max/Pro/Team/Ultra snapshot are no longer misclassified as quota-unavailable, which used to erase the snapshot and set `knownLimitsAvailability` to `.unavailable`.
2. **Repeated CLI parse failures** are now treated as preservable failures when prior data exists, so the card keeps showing stale data while the failure gate still surfaces the error after the gate threshold.

Education / no-prior-data behavior is unchanged: those cases still drop the snapshot and show "Limits not available".

## Test plan

- `swift test --filter Issue2241ReproTests` — added new regression tests that fail on current main and pass with this change.
- `swift test --filter ClaudeResilienceTests` — includes new repeated CLI parse failure case.
- `swift test --filter ClaudeEducationAvailabilityTests` — includes new subscription-only response with prior subscription limits case.

## Compatibility

Low. The change only affects Claude refresh failure publication when a prior snapshot already exists. It does not alter other providers or the Education/no-prior-data path.
